title: Why I start backend design from failure cases
summary: I start most backend design sessions by mapping what can fail first, then I shape APIs and queues around those boundaries.
points: I define timeout, retry, and fallback behavior before I add business logic.
I separate synchronous API paths from asynchronous event processing as early as possible.
I add structured logs up front because I think observability is a core feature, not an afterthought.

title: What Kafka taught me about service boundaries
summary: Using event streams helped me reduce tight coupling between services and make deployments less risky.
points: I use events to communicate state changes instead of direct service-to-service dependency chains.
I keep event contracts explicit with versioning because I want to avoid downstream breakages.
I treat idempotency as a first-class requirement in consumers because duplicate events are unavoidable in real systems.

title: How I keep AI workflows controllable with LangGraph
summary: In my experience, agentic systems become easier to trust when every step is explicit, reviewable, and resumable.
points: I use a plan → approval → execution flow for sensitive tool actions.
I store checkpoints so interrupted sessions can resume cleanly.
I add structured JSON outputs and logs because I care about clear post-run analysis.

title: Guardrails I apply to public AI chat features
summary: I believe public assistants need strict scope control, rate limits, and safer defaults to stay useful in production.
points: I limit assistant scope to portfolio topics and ignore unrelated misuse attempts.
I apply rate limits and optional API token checks on expensive endpoints.
I use redacted logging by default outside development environments because privacy matters.

title: From internship tasks to production ownership
summary: I shifted from implementing assigned tasks to taking responsibility for reliability, traceability, and long-term maintenance impact.
points: I balance delivery speed with long-term maintainability decisions.
I write clearer docs because I want to reduce support and onboarding friction.
I treat observability and error handling as part of core feature delivery.

title: Docker + .env lessons from VPS deployment
summary: I learned that small formatting issues in env files can silently break startup behavior in containers.
points: I avoid inline comments on env value lines when using docker --env-file.
I keep numeric values unquoted where possible to reduce parser surprises.
I verify runtime env values inside containers before doing deeper debugging.
